subject.title: [Bug]: Native Talk button triggers OpenAI Realtime WebRTC call and fails with 500 when Realtime is not configured

question: Should Control UI browser Talk start when a realtime provider is implicitly available through OpenAI/Codex auth, or should it require explicit Gateway realtime readiness before microphone/WebRTC startup?
rationale: Current code starts the client-owned realtime path from the Talk button, while current docs and recent merges allow broader OpenAI/Codex auth availability; either policy affects user setup semantics and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Gate on Gateway readiness
options.body: Use talk.catalog/readiness or an equivalent Gateway preflight to disable or block Talk before microphone startup while preserving the chosen credential policy.

options.title: Keep implicit auth activation
options.body: Accept that OpenAI/Codex realtime credential availability enables browser Talk and focus the remaining work on clearer provider/API error messages.

options.title: Require explicit realtime config
options.body: Only start browser Talk when talk.realtime is explicitly configured, with upgrade proof for users who currently rely on implicit auth availability.

recommendation.title: Gate on Gateway readiness
recommendation.body: Use talk.catalog/readiness or an equivalent Gateway preflight to disable or block Talk before microphone startup while preserving the chosen credential policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent OpenAI Realtime/Codex auth and Control UI Talk ownership make this the closest current decision owner from the history trail.
